title: Vinyl Plank Flooring Trends for 2026: Widths, Colors and Patterns
meta: 2026 vinyl plank trends: wider planks, pale and warm oak tones, matte texture and herringbone. Wills Flooring in Lynnwood shows what lasts and what to skip.
keywords: vinyl plank flooring trends 2026, LVP colors 2026, wide plank vinyl flooring, herringbone vinyl plank, vinyl plank flooring Lynnwood WA, best vinyl plank color for resale

blocks.lead: For 2026, vinyl plank is going wider (7 to 9 inches), longer (60 inches and up), lighter and warmer in color, with low-gloss embossed texture, and herringbone and mixed-width layouts are back in a serious way.
blocks.detail: Those are the planks leaving our Lynnwood showroom van most often this year. Wills Flooring installs any of them for $2.50 per sq ft of labor, with the plank itself quoted separately at the free in-home estimate.

blocks.html: Most people who book a mobile showroom visit in Lynnwood open the door holding a phone with a saved photo. In 2026 that photo is almost always a wide, pale, matte plank in an open kitchen, often with a herringbone entry. This post covers what is actually trending in vinyl plank, what each trend costs in extra material and labor, and which trends hold up in the 1960s to 1980s ramblers and split-levels around Alderwood, Meadowdale and Martha Lake. For the full service picture, start with our vinyl plank installation page.

blocks.text: Widths and lengths: the plank keeps getting bigger

items.title: 7 to 9 inch widths are the new normal
items.text: Five years ago 6 inches was wide. In 2026 the samples people pick are 7, 8 and 9 inches. Wider planks mean fewer seams, so the floor reads calmer and closer to real wide-plank hardwood. They also show every subfloor bump, which matters in older Lynnwood homes.

items.title: 60 to 72 inch lengths
items.text: Longer planks cut the number of end joints in a room by a third or more. In a 20 ft living room that is the difference between a floor that looks like flooring and one that looks like a floor. Waste goes up slightly, which shows in the material quote.

items.title: Mixed-width packs
items.text: Cartons that mix 5, 7 and 9 inch planks are the most requested new format at our showroom this year. The random look copies reclaimed and European oak floors. Installation takes longer because the pattern has to be planned so widths do not clump.

items.title: Large-format tile looks
items.text: Vinyl in 12 by 24 and 18 by 36 inch stone and concrete looks is trending for kitchens, laundry rooms and entries. It pairs with plank elsewhere and avoids the cold feet of real tile in a Lynnwood winter.

blocks.text: Texture, gloss and bevel: the small details that date a floor

items.html: Matte and ultra-matte finishes. The biggest shift. Gloss vinyl looks like vinyl under Lynnwood's flat winter light and shows every scuff. Low-sheen finishes read as oiled wood.
Embossed-in-register texture. The grain you feel lines up with the grain you see. Cheaper plank stamps a generic texture over an unrelated print, and you can tell from standing height.
Painted micro-bevels. A small, painted bevel defines each plank without the deep V-groove that collected dirt on 2015-era floors. Square-edge planks are trending in tile looks.
Fewer repeating boards. Better collections print 30 or more unique boards per pattern. If you can spot the same knot twice in a hallway, the collection is too small.

blocks.title: The Lynnwood subfloor reality:
blocks.text: Many Alderwood and Meadowdale homes from the 1960s and 70s have plywood or particleboard over joists that have settled unevenly. The wider the plank, the more that shows as rocking joints and visible dips. Trendy width is fine, but budget for floor leveling first. We check flatness with a straightedge at the free estimate and quote any prep separately.
How to pick a trend you will still like in 2036

items.html: Look at the sample in your own light, at 4 pm in January. Lynnwood winter light is gray and low. A pale plank that glowed in a store can look flat at home. That is exactly why we bring the samples to you.
Match the trim and cabinets, not the photo. Warm oak cabinets and pale gray-oak plank fight. Warm honey plank makes the same kitchen look intentional.
Check flatness before falling for wide plank. Ask us to put a 10 ft straightedge on the floor. If there are gaps over 3/16 in, the leveling cost belongs in your decision.

Use pattern in one room, not everywhere. A herringbone entry or dining room reads as a feature. A whole house of it reads as effort, and it costs more in material and labor. Our herringbone vinyl plank guide covers the details.
Buy the spec, not the trend. A 20 mil wear layer, a rigid core and a collection with 30 plus unique boards will still look good when the color trend has moved on.

faq.q: What is the most popular vinyl plank color in 2026?
faq.a: Pale to warm natural oak with low color variation and a matte finish. It has led for three years because it looks like lightly finished real wood, brightens rooms during gray Northwest winters, hides dust well and fits both modern and traditional Lynnwood homes.

faq.q: Is gray vinyl plank flooring out of style?
faq.a: Cool gray and silvery whitewashed planks are out for new installs in 2026. Greige is still acceptable but reads as a few years old. If you like gray, choose a warm taupe-oak rather than a true gray so the floor does not date the whole house.

It looks more like real wide-plank hardwood and has fewer seams, which most people prefer. The trade-off is that wide planks show subfloor dips and can rock at the joints over uneven floors, common in older Lynnwood ramblers. Check flatness first and level where needed.

faq.q: Does herringbone vinyl plank cost more to install?
faq.a: Yes. Herringbone uses special short planks, needs a flatter subfloor, takes more layout time and produces around 15 percent waste instead of 7 to 10 percent. Wills Flooring's base rate is $2.50 per sq ft for standard installation; pattern layouts are quoted at the free estimate.

faq.q: Which vinyl plank trend is best for resale in Lynnwood?
faq.a: A wide, matte, light-to-warm oak plank in a straight lay through the main living areas. It photographs well, matches the widest range of cabinets and paint, and is what buyers in Lynnwood's growing light-rail neighborhoods currently expect to see.

faq.q: Should I match my vinyl plank to my existing hardwood?
faq.a: Do not try for an exact match; it never quite works and the mismatch looks accidental. Either pick a plank that is clearly lighter or darker as a deliberate contrast, or use a transition strip at a doorway and treat the two floors as separate rooms.
